abstract: Breast and ovarian cancers share molecular alterations that may reveal common therapeutic targets. Here, we integrated six Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) datasets to identify shared transcriptional changes across the two cancers. Independent differential expression analysis followed by direction-specific intersection identified 396 shared differentially expressed genes (DEGs), comprising 192 upregulated and 204 downregulated genes. Protein-protein interaction analysis prioritized ten hub genes: AURKA, AURKB, BCL2, BIRC5, CCNA2, CDK1, FOXO1, KIF11, PTEN, and TOP2A. Functional enrichment highlighted cell-cycle regulation, mitotic spindle organization, and p53-associated signalling. Independent expression assessment using GEPIA2 identified seven hub genes significantly upregulated in both cancers, while FOXO1 was downregulated. Regulatory network analysis further identified candidate transcription factors and miRNAs potentially associated with these hubs. For therapeutic exploration, a 70,478-compound FooDB library was progressively filtered to 233 candidates using physicochemical, structural-alert, machine-learning-based bioactivity, and ADMET criteria. Molecular docking against eight selected druggable hubs, followed by decoy benchmarking and 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, prioritized three complexes: CDK1-artonin L, AURKB-taraxacin, and KIF11-L-thyronine. CDK1-artonin L demonstrated the strongest overall computational support, whereas the AURKB and KIF11 complexes showed differing levels of binding and energetic evidence. This study provides an integrated multi-cohort framework for identifying shared molecular hubs in breast and ovarian cancer and prioritizing food-derived compounds for further investigation. The findings nominate CDK1, AURKB, and KIF11 for experimental evaluation.
